evals.prompt: brief me on resources/human-level-ai-review.md, I don't have time to read the whole thing
evals.expected_output: A brief file beside the paper with TL;DR, structure map, chunk summaries, claims with anchors and statuses, risks, least-confident block; sequential path (3 chunks).
expectations: Output brief.md exists and contains sections TL;DR, Claims, Risks, Least confident
Every claim row has a source anchor (line number or heading)
Each claim carries a status of verified, unverified, or contradicted
Brief is at most 1/3 the word count of the source (about 1066 words of 3200)
TL;DR has 5 or fewer bullets and names the comprehension bottleneck thesis

evals.prompt: summarize evals/fixtures/ledger-design.md for me and flag anything that doesn't add up
evals.expected_output: Fan-out path (4+ chunks). Brief flags the 30 second vs 90 second risk engine timeout as contradicted with both anchors.
expectations: Brief flags the risk-engine timeout as contradicted (30 seconds vs 90 seconds)
The contradiction cites both locations (Timeouts and retries section and Operations section)
Output brief.md has sections TL;DR, Claims, Risks, Least confident
Brief is at most 1500 words (1/3 of source, capped)

evals.prompt: what does the diff since 5e3c12b~3 actually change? too big to read
evals.expected_output: Brief for git diff with code/diff chunks, high-risk chunks listed first, claims anchored to file:line.
expectations: Output brief.md covers the diff with per-file or per-chunk summaries anchored to file paths
High-risk chunks or files (scripts, tests, fixtures with subprocess/open) are listed before low-risk prose
Brief states at least one behavior claim with an anchor of the form path:line
Brief includes a least-confident or uncertainty statement
Brief is at most 1500 words, because a brief longer than the reader can absorb in one sitting defeats its purpose
